title: Lazy Daddy Fillmore and Bunk's soft, sweet trumpet
summary: Brief talk of Lazy Daddy Fillmore, then Bunk's band and his soft, sweet playing compared with Bolden and Keppard.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Did you ever run into Lazy Daddy, a piano player over there? Lazy Daddy Fillmore, they called him. The Bunkers used to talk about him. Other people say he's dead now. Yeah. Did you hear him? Did you ever play with him?
No, I never played with him. I wasn't.
I wanted to go down in the recording, but before I could find Barry Rubs, I heard he was dead. Yeah. He'd been down in Corpus Christi for a while.
Mm-hmm. He had a good band. Bunker had a good band. He was the worst one in the band.
Yeah, he could play, but he wouldn't play after that. That's how he played about.
Well his teeth were gone, I guess, and he couldn't do so well maybe then.

Uh-uh. Eddie wasn't about the teeth that much. It wasn't that. Eddie never was no loud trumpet player, you know. He used to play soft and sweet. Low, you know. Yeah. All the way he had his own teeth. He used to clean up all of them for that.
He never, that's what I always heard too. He wasn't really powerful. No.

But he could play. Like Bolden or Keppard. No, but he could play, I'm telling you, I'm supposed to scale it. Marlon. I was talking with him. He said, you got to do watching, I drew. You coming out good. Watch, you watch your, the only one I'm telling you to watch, I watch it. I, I, I don't know. I said, you see that there's a bunk there? I said, yeah. Oh, I said, he can play, man. He can make some stuff, he said. But I said, you got to watch. You got to watch your, the only one I watch you. I, I scared nobody but him. I mean, he could play. He's a good finger, you know, he had good fingers.
